# 06. Design System

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Create reusable standards that keep static sites consistent, maintainable, accessible, and fast.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A token set for color, type, spacing, radius, shadow, z-index, duration, easing, and breakpoints.
- [ ] A component catalog with purpose, anatomy, variants, states, accessibility rules, and content constraints.
- [ ] A CSS architecture rule for custom properties, cascade layers, naming, file structure, and override policy.
- [ ] A responsive behavior rule for each component, including wrapping, stacking, hiding, and overflow.
- [ ] A motion standard that respects prefers-reduced-motion and avoids essential motion-only meaning.
- [ ] A form pattern library covering labels, help text, required fields, validation, consent, success, and error states.
- [ ] A content pattern library for hero, proof, service detail, feature lists, pricing, FAQ, testimonials, case studies, and legal notices.
- [ ] A versioning rule so changes to shared components can be audited across static pages.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Design tokens must be named by role, not by raw color or one-off visual description.
- [ ] Components must support keyboard focus, screen reader names, reduced motion, and responsive text.
- [ ] Shared CSS must not force every site into the same visual personality.
- [ ] Component variants must exist only when they represent real semantic or functional differences.
- [ ] Utility classes must not become a replacement for readable component structure where maintainability suffers.
- [ ] The system must work without proprietary design-system runtime packages.
- [ ] CSS custom properties must have sensible fallbacks where failure would harm readability.
- [ ] Design system documentation must include what not to use, not only approved patterns.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check that every color token has contrast-tested pairings.
- [ ] Check that every component state is implemented in CSS and appears in at least one QA page or fixture.
- [ ] Check that shared components do not require JavaScript unless the behavior demands it.
- [ ] Check that component markup uses native HTML elements before ARIA patterns.
- [ ] Check that icons, images, and embedded media have accessible naming rules.
- [ ] Check that global resets do not remove focus outlines, list semantics, button affordance, or form usability.
- [ ] Check that CSS is organized for deletion and reuse, not only addition.
- [ ] Check that templates can be copied into a new static site without external paid dependencies.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid token names such as blue-1 when the color's role is action, link, border, or accent.
- [ ] Avoid component APIs that require developers to memorize invisible rules.
- [ ] Avoid excessive shadows, radii, animations, or gradients as substitutes for hierarchy.
- [ ] Avoid duplicating components with tiny visual differences.
- [ ] Avoid global CSS selectors that unexpectedly alter third-party embeds or content markdown.
- [ ] Avoid design tokens that are documented but not used in production CSS.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] A new page must be buildable from existing patterns without visual drift.
- [ ] The system must make the accessible path the easiest path.
- [ ] The CSS must be understandable by another front-end developer without a proprietary editor.
- [ ] Design system quality must be proven by responsive, real-content examples.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use static audits to flag missing focus CSS, repeated hard-coded colors, missing component states, and absent design tokens where project conventions define them.
- [ ] Use linting with free tools when a project adds npm-based workflows.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Consistency rules cover colors, type scale, spacing, buttons, cards, icons, forms, section padding, borders, shadows, radius, and interaction states.
- [ ] Brand expression rules ensure the system feels unique, appropriate to industry and price point, memorable, high quality, and free of random decorative choices.
- [ ] Component quality rules cover clickable buttons, balanced cards, trustworthy forms, credible testimonials, polished logo areas, consistent image treatments, intentional dividers, accessible accordions/tabs/modals, and useful controls.
- [ ] Design tokens and components protect future pages from visual drift while allowing content-specific variation.
- [ ] CMS/no-code guardrails protect global fonts, colors, spacing, buttons, cards, header, footer, breakpoints, motion, and core layout from unsafe casual editing.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
